facts.text: Sigourney was founded in 1844 and named after the beloved poet Lydia Sigourney, who later helped fund tree planting in the town’s courtyard.
The Keokuk County Historical Society, located at 402 East Elm Street, preserves the region’s past through a vast collection of photographs, artifacts, and genealogy records.
Sigourney’s historic courthouse square, home to the Keokuk County Courthouse, is a centerpiece of the town’s public square historic district.
The Community History Archives offers free, digitized access to newspapers from 1870 to 2023, letting residents and researchers explore the town’s stories online.
Sigourney’s charming historic downtown features a mix of preserved 19th‑century architecture and lively community events that celebrate the town’s agricultural heritage.
